title: Finish the harness

tests.expect:
static int32_t b0[3] = {10, 20, 0}; | kernel(b0); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[0]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[1]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[2]);

static int32_t b0[1] = {7}; | static int32_t b1[2] = {0, 0}; | kernel(b0, b1); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[0]); | printf("1 %d
", (int)b1[0]); | printf("1 %d
", (int)b1[1]);

static int32_t b0[2] = {-1, 2}; | static int32_t b1[1] = {3}; | static int32_t b2[2] = {4, 5}; | kernel(b0, b1, b2); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[0]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[1]); | printf("1 %d
", (int)b1[0]); | printf("2 %d
", (int)b2[0]); | printf("2 %d
", (int)b2[1]);

static int32_t b0[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0}; | kernel(b0); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[0]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[1]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[2]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[3]);

static int32_t b2[1] = {9}; | static int32_t b5[2] = {8, -7}; | kernel(b2, b5); | printf("2 %d
", (int)b2[0]); | printf("5 %d
", (int)b5[0]); | printf("5 %d
", (int)b5[1]);

hints: The call needs one name per buffer: `b0`, `b1` and so on. Build each name from `slot` with `Printf.sprintf "b%d"`, then join them with `String.concat ", "`.
The prints come after the call. For one buffer, `List.mapi (fun i _ -> print_line slot i) data` gives its lines. `List.concat_map` does that for every buffer and joins the results.
Return `List.map decl bufs @ [call] @ prints`, where `call` is `"kernel(" ^ String.concat ", " names ^ ");"`.
explain: A harness is three groups of lines: one array per buffer filled with its starting data, one call to `kernel` with the arrays in slot order, and one print per element. The prints must come after the call, because the kernel changes the arrays in place.
